newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds remain firm in late trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds remain firm in late trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities registered healthy gains in thin trade on Tuesday, following a market-friendly report on consumer prices earlier in the day, traders said.
But light mortgage banker selling and investor demand for Treasury paper widened pass-through yield spreads moderately, they said.
"We saw some mortgage banker selling out of the chute," said one pass-through trader. "We did see some decent institutional two-way flow in 7.0-percent and 7.5-percent conventionals," he said.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0-percent paper was up 13/32 at 100-28/32, yielding 110 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 13/32 higher as well, at 100-29/32 and 101-03/32, respectively.
Five-year Treasuries were up 13/32 at 6.76 percent, and 10-year notes were up 24/32 at 6.87 percent.

The Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.1 percent with the "core" rate, excluding volatile food and energy components, up 0.2 percent. Consensus estimates had seen CPI up 0.2 percent, the core up 0.3 percent.
